requirements.requirement: node3 has a single gateway address for reaching node4
requirements.summary: node3's eth1 route table shows a single static route to 10.10.20.0/24 via 10.10.10.254, the VRRP VIP shared by node1/node2, confirmed both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Gateway prefers node1 while node1 is healthy
requirements.summary: node1 configured with VRRP priority 200 vs node2's 100; show vrrp confirms node1 MASTER and node2 BACKUP on both groups NET-A/NET-B in the healthy baseline and after full restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Gateway/connectivity stays available when node1 (preferred router) is down
requirements.summary: node1's eth1/eth2 links were brought down; node2 was confirmed promoted to MASTER on both VRRP groups within seconds, and node3->node4 ping continued with 0% packet loss during the outage.

requirements.requirement: Gateway/connectivity stays available when node2 (backup router) is down
requirements.summary: node2 was rebooted as part of the mandatory restart protocol while node1 was master, but no ping to node4 was captured during node2's outage window (unlike the explicit node1-down test). Since node1 remaining master during node2's absence is the normal/expected state rather than a failover event, this scenario is only indirectly evidenced.

requirements.requirement: node1 reclaims MASTER (preferred router) once it becomes healthy again
requirements.summary: After node1's links were restored, show vrrp confirms node1 became MASTER again (priority 200) on both groups, node2 returned to BACKUP, and node3->node4 connectivity remained intact.

overall_summary: The executor configured VRRP (NET-A/NET-B) on node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100) providing a single floating VIP gateway (10.10.10.254) that node3 uses to reach node4, and demonstrated node1-down failover to node2 with continuous connectivity, followed by preemption back to node1. All four nodes were restarted per the mandatory protocol with verified boot-identity change and recovered VRRP/IP/route state. The only gap is that the node2-down (backup router) failure scenario was not explicitly exercised with a live ping during outage, though node2 was rebooted and recovered correctly.
limitations: No ping-during-outage evidence was captured for the node2 restart window, so the 'backup router down' failover path is only indirectly evidenced via VRRP-group state, not a live traffic test.

VyOS 'show configuration commands' introspection failed repeatedly early in the session due to shell/vbash syntax issues; the executor fell back to 'run show vrrp'/'run show interfaces', which provided sufficient evidence but full running-config text was never captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor's state-changing commands map cleanly to task requirements: VRRP/interface configuration on node1/node2 (committed and saved), static IP/route configuration on node3/node4 via nmcli, a bounded link-down/link-up test on node1's eth1/eth2 (fully restored within the same session, used to demonstrate failover and preemption), and the mandatory sequential reboot of all four nodes with pre/post verification. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; failed commands (29 of 89) were read-only diagnostic/discovery attempts (e.g. failed 'show configuration commands' syntax probes, transient connection-timeout polling during reboots) that did not mutate state.
